title: Improving NL→Formal-Spec Semantic Correctness via Constrained Prompting plus Verifier Feedback (Preregistered, Repair)
research_question: Does combining constrained prompting with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase the semantic-correctness rate of translating operator natural-language intents into formal network specifications compared to baseline prompting?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Constrained prompting (structured templates + explicit semantic slots) increases NL→formal-spec semantic-correctness versus unconstrained baseline prompting.
H2: Adding deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair) further increases semantic-correctness versus constrained prompting alone.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which intent types (reachability, isolation, ACL, QoS) benefit most from verifier feedback and how do revision counts vary by type?
EQ2: What common syntactic or semantic failure modes remain after verifier-feedback repair?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic, programmatically generated operator intents covering four intent families: reachability, isolation, ACL-change, QoS constraint.
Topology sizes restricted to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes) generated deterministically by the preregistered topology generator.
Confirmatory claims are strictly about performance on the sampled synthetic intent corpus and verifier-harness; no claim of production-network generalization is made.
model_scope: A single hosted LLM API (identifier recorded at execution) called under fixed-seed / fixed-session isolation per intent-condition.
Deterministic prompting templates and fixed generation sampling parameters (temperature set to nominal low value per preregistration).
No human-in-the-loop scoring, annotation, or manual adjudication will be used.
transformation_scope: Templates that map NL intents to a canonical formal-spec surface (formal language compatible with the preregistered verifier).
Deterministic translator wrappers that produce verifier input (no manual mapping).
Automated mapping code (published) that transforms model outputs to verifier input; ambiguous/parse-failure outputs are handled automatically per the ambiguity rules below.
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents programmatically generated (50 per intent-family target balance post-ambiguity-filter). For each intent, run three translation conditions (A: baseline free-text prompt, B: constrained template prompt, C: constrained prompt + verifier-feedback loop). Inclusion rule: intents that trigger deterministic ambiguity-detection (see ambiguity rules) are excluded from confirmatory set and routed to exploratory corpus. Exclusion is deterministic, code-published, and applied prior to any model call. Each intent-condition pair is executed in an isolated model session with fixed seed/state reset. Max verifier-feedback iterations per intent in condition C: 3 model calls (initial + up to 2 repairs); average-expected iterations assumed 2 for budgeting. Randomization: none required (paired within-intent design). All intent IDs and topology seeds are published.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary comparison of semantic-correctness (verifier pass/fail) between Condition C (guarded) and Condition A (baseline) using the supplied paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (McNemar-style paired-proportion test with bootstrap CIs). Secondary analyses: paired tests B vs A and C vs B with Bonferroni correction across these two secondary contrasts. Report absolute percentage-point differences, odds ratios, exact two-sided p-values, and 95% bootstrap CIs (10,000 bootstrap resamples). For condition C report median and IQR of revision iterations. Missing/incomplete pairs: primary treatment is 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs for primary analysis); sensitivity analysis will run 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treating failed/missing guarded outputs as failures (zero) to bound effects. All analysis code, seeds, and raw verifier verdicts are published.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: single primary contrast (C vs A) at alpha=0.05 (two-sided). Secondary confirmatory contrasts (B vs A and C vs B): familywise alpha adjusted via Bonferroni for these two tests (each at alpha=0.025 two-sided). Exploratory contrasts (subgroups, error taxonomy) are explicitly labeled exploratory and not used for confirmatory claims.
missingness_plan: Model/API timeouts or parsing failures are logged and trigger deterministic retry policy: one automatic retry after fixed backoff; if still failing, mark the model-call as failed. For the primary analysis incomplete intent-condition pairs are removed (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analysis treats failed guarded outputs as failures (zero) and reports results. All failed-call counts, causes, and hashes are published.

benchmark_names: Preregistered synthetic NL→formal-spec corpus v1 (this study)
risk_factors: Prompt-history or session-state leakage across runs
Model nondeterminism in hosted API responses
Verifier parser/translation bugs that could mis-evaluate semantic correctness
Ambiguous intents that legitimately permit multiple correct formalizations
detection_procedures: Session isolation enforced by fresh API session/token per intent-condition; automated session-hash verification to detect leakage.
Duplicate-response and response-entropy checks; if identical outputs repeated across seeds suspicious runs are flagged automatically.
Deterministic unit-tests for mapping code and verifier-input transformations run before batch evaluation; failing unit-tests cause automated abort of the run.
Ambiguity detection: rule-based parser (published) that flags underspecified intents prior to model calling.
item_flagging_rules: If verifier-input mapping fails to parse, automatically mark the item as 'parse_failure' and exclude from confirmatory set.
If ambiguity-detection returns true, classify intent as 'ambiguous' and place into exploratory corpus (excluded from confirmatory analysis).
If verifier reports 'unsupported-feature' for an intent, exclude that intent from confirmatory set and record as excluded with deterministic reason code.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: All flagged/ excluded items are reported with counts and deterministic reasons. Confirmatory analysis uses only items that pass parser, ambiguity, and verifier-coverage checks. Sensitivity analyses reintroduce excluded items where feasible by mapping them to reduced invariants (documented transformation).
residual_uncertainty: Verifier coverage gaps for production-scale invariants (addressed by exclusion but residuals reported).
Model API nondeterminism affecting variance estimates (quantified via repeated-seed exploratory runs).

budget_scenarios.description: Primary recommend: N=150 confirmatory intents, exploratory corpus 50 intents. Average verifier-feedback calls per C assumed = 2 (initial + 1 repair). One model call per intent for A and B. 10% overhead budgeted for retries/logging.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call budget (660) is well below capability manifest limit (max 10000); CPU and docker resources suffice for verifier and mapping code execution; all datasets are synthetic/programmatic so no human annotation is required.

budget_scenarios.description: Reduced budget confirmatory run: N=80 confirmatory intents to conserve API spend; exploratory corpus 40 intents. Same per-intent call assumptions and 10% retry overhead.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Smaller confirmatory set reduces power but remains executable under compute limits and is useful as a pilot; all exclusions and deterministic pre-filters remain identical.

budget_scenarios.description: Scale-up confirmatory run (optional if additional budget available): N=300 confirmatory intents; exploratory 100 intents; same per-intent assumptions; 10% overhead.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Still below manifest model-call cap; useful for tighter CIs if budget permits.

power_plan.target_effect: Detect absolute increase of 15 percentage points (e.g., baseline 35% → guarded 50%) with 80% power at alpha=0.05 for primary contrast (C vs A).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired-proportion (McNemar-style) power calculation using conservative discordant-pair proportion assumption (discordant rate ≈ 0.30). Analytical calculation indicates N≈132; rounded up to N=150 for buffer; sensitivity via bootstrap simulation under varying baseline (25–45%) and discordant rates (0.20–0.40).
assumptions: Two-sided alpha=0.05 for primary contrast; secondary contrasts Bonferroni-adjusted.
Guarded condition mean iterations per item ≈ 2 for budgeting.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=150 the design has ≈80% power to detect ~15 percentage-point absolute difference under stated assumptions; smaller effects (e.g., 8–10 pp) would be underpowered; sensitivity analyses report MDE across assumed baseline rates.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power/numeric CIs under baseline rates 25%, 35%, 45%.
Bootstrap power simulation varying discordant-pair rates 0.20–0.40 (report contour plot).
Secondary analysis: treat failed/missing guarded outputs as failures (sensitivity lower bound).

transformation_families: Structured prompt templates (slot-filling) with deterministic token positions
Automated mapping code from LLM output to verifier input (parser + sanitizer)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Deterministic verifier harness (NetKAT/KATch family referenced in evidence) executes concrete scenario tests constructed from the intent generator; pass/fail verdicts are deterministic given mapping inputs.
Unit tests validating mapping transformations against 100 deterministic seed cases (published).
End-to-end smoke tests for each topology size and intent family recorded with hashes.
automatic_rejection_rules: Parser failure: automatic exclusion from confirmatory set and record as 'parse_failure'.
Ambiguity-detection true: automatic exclusion to exploratory set with deterministic reason code.
Unsupported verifier feature: automatic exclusion or fallback to reduced invariant mapping (documented transformation).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Publish an automated audit sample of 20% of confirmatory items (random deterministic seed) containing model outputs, mapping inputs, and verifier logs for external reproducibility checks (no human adjudication).
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Mapping code includes deterministic grammar-based parser with unit-test coverage >95% on preregistered seed set; failing cases abort run and are reported.
residual_risks: Verifier expressiveness may not cover some real-world invariants; such intents are excluded deterministically.
Mapping code bugs could systematically alter semantics; mitigated by unit-tests and pre-run acceptance checks but residual implementation risk remains.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity: results are limited to the synthetic programmatic corpus and verifier-harness; production-network heterogeneity and scale remain untested.

Choice of a single hosted LLM API means observed effect sizes may not generalize across models; sensitivity analysis on seeds and prompt variants will be reported but multi-model generality is not claimed.
Verifier-family selection (NetKAT/KATch) favors invariants expressible in that formalism; other invariants may require alternate verifiers and are out of scope.
Hosted API nondeterminism contributes to variance estimates; repeated exploratory runs quantify this but cannot remove it entirely.
